concepts.def: Lens opening controlling light and depth of field; measured in f-stops.
Length of time the sensor is exposed to light; affects motion blur.
Sensor sensitivity to light; higher ISO allows lower light but adds noise.
Arrangement of elements in a photograph; rule of thirds, leading lines.
Early photographic process (1842) producing Prussian-blue prints; revived by contemporary artists.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Photography and Lens-based Media — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Photography and Lens-based Media brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Photography and Lens-based Media.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
